title: Predicting Protein-Protein Interactions Using Vectorized Sequence Descriptors and Machine Learning Classifiers
authors: Ruchika Bhat; Vaishnavi Kumari; Virendra Singh Kaira; Zakeerhussain D Kudari; Sai P. Shankar; G. Jaiganesh
one_liner_zh: 用序列衍生特征（AC/CT/LD）结合SVM/RF/XGBoost预测蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用，属于蛋白质相互作用预测而非结构计算建模，方法为传统机器学习且无结构层面贡献。
abstract: Accurate prediction of protein-protein interactions (PPIs) is fundamental for elucidating cellular mechanisms and accelerating drug discovery. Although experimental techniques provide extensive interaction maps, their high cost and time requirements necessitate robust computational alternatives. In this study, we present an interpretable machine-learning framework that integrates sequence-derived descriptors,specifically 120 Auto-Covariance (AC) features, 686 Conjoint Triad (CT) features, and 1,820 Local Descriptors (LD) features, with classical classification algorithms, including Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forests (RF), and XGBoost (XGB). Evaluated on gold-standard sequence-based PPI benchmark dataset using stratified five fold cross-validation, the models achieved robust classification accuracies: 86.92% (SVM), 97.75% (RF), and a peak cross-validation accuracy of 97.97% with XGBoost (Rec: 98.09%, Pr: 98.10%, F1: 98.09%). Furthermore, rigorous evaluation on an independent unseen (Human-PPI) test set demonstrated exceptional generalization capabilities. The Random Forest model emerged as the top-performing architecture, yielding an outstanding accuracy of 99.51%, a precision of 99.72%, a recall of 99.29%, an F1-score of 99.50%, an Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.9990, and an Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve (AUPRC) of 0.9989 (closely followed by XGBoost with 98.54% accuracy, AUROC 0.9979, and AUPRC 0.9974). Feature-importance analysis revealed that short-range physicochemical correlations (such as polarity and hydrophobicity lags in Protein 2), regional amino-acid compositions, and specific triad patterns (e.g., A/G/V-M/S/T/Y-M/S/T/Y) drive accurate PPI discrimination. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of domain-informed, handcrafted sequence features combined with machine-learning classifiers for PPI prediction, providing biologically interpretable insights with minimal computational overhead and enabling efficient, scalable interactome screening.
abstract_zh: 准确预测蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（protein-protein interactions, PPIs）是阐明细胞机制和加速药物发现的基础。尽管实验技术提供了广泛的相互作用图谱，但其高成本和时间需求使得稳健的计算替代方法成为必要。在本研究中，我们提出了一个可解释的机器学习框架，该框架将序列衍生的描述符，具体包括120个自协方差（Auto-Covariance, AC）特征、686个联合三元组（Conjoint Triad, CT）特征和1,820个局部描述符（Local Descriptors, LD）特征，与经典分类算法相结合，包括支持向量机（Support Vector Machines, SVM）、随机森林（Random Forests, RF）和XGBoost（XGB）。在基于序列的PPI金标准基准数据集上使用分层五折交叉验证进行评估，模型取得了稳健的分类准确率：86.92%（SVM）、97.75%（RF），以及XGBoost的峰值交叉验证准确率97.97%（Rec: 98.09%, Pr: 98.10%, F1: 98.09%）。此外，在一个独立的未见（Human-PPI）测试集上的严格评估展示了卓越的泛化能力。随机森林模型成为表现最佳的架构，取得了出色的准确率99.51%、精确率99.72%、召回率99.29%、F1分数99.50%、受试者工作特征曲线下面积（Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve, AUROC）0.9990，以及精确率-召回率曲线下面积（Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve, AUPRC）0.9989（紧随其后的是XGBoost，准确率98.54%、AUROC 0.9979、AUPRC 0.9974）。特征重要性分析揭示，短程理化相关性（如蛋白质2中的极性和疏水性滞后）、区域氨基酸组成以及特定三元组模式（例如A/G/V-M/S/T/Y-M/S/T/Y）驱动了准确的PPI判别。这些发现证明了领域知识驱动的手工序列特征与机器学习分类器相结合在PPI预测中的有效性，提供了具有生物学可解释性的见解，且计算开销极小，能够实现高效、可扩展的相互作用组筛选。
